coverage.summary: Statewide just-cause rule for residential real property, including units in mobilehome parks, after 12 months of occupancy. Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years is exempt, as are the listed categories. Property covered by a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept. 1, 2019, or by a more protective later ordinance, follows the local ordinance instead. A property is never subject to both.
coverage.owner_conditions: The separately alienable property exemption requires a non-corporate, non-REIT owner and the written notice. The owner-occupied duplex exemption lasts only while the owner remains in occupancy.
coverage.other_conditions: A local ordinance adopted after Sept. 1, 2019 that is less protective than this section is not enforced unless this section is repealed. Does not apply to homeowners of mobilehomes.

result.notes: Changed requires_unknown_facts from true to false. The section covers ordinary residential real property; the affordable-housing, separately-alienable and owner-occupancy carve-outs are exemptions an address lookup cannot check, and they are already listed in unverifiable_exemptions. Set may_preempt_local_rules to true because subd. (i)(3) bars enforcement of less protective local ordinances adopted after Sept. 1, 2019. Removed the named example ordinances (LA, San Francisco, Berkeley, San Diego, Santa Ana) from the summary because no document supports them. construction_cutoff stays null: the 15-year certificate-of-occupancy exemption is a rolling window, not a fixed date, so it is captured in new_construction_exemption and min_building_age_years (whose basis is the certificate of occupancy, not year built). requires_owner_filing=false rests on the exemption applying by its own terms, with no filing step anywhere in subd. (e)(7).
